title: Private Console: Canary-Sensitive Egress Budgeting Cards & Incident-aware Rollout Shield
creator: Ethan Clark
description: Design a compact, actionable status strip and set of cards for Private/VPC clusters that surface egress budget consumption in real time and integrate with Canary Rollout safeguards. The goal is to help SREs and tenant owners detect when an in-progress canary might cause network egress overspend or cross-region throttling, and to offer immediate rollback/freeze actions plus a lightweight incident playbook. This ticket covers flow sketches, high-fidelity card variants, accessibility pass, and handoff artifacts for engineering and PM. Considerations: show per-tenant and aggregated cluster egress, forecast burn rate, map to billing buckets, and expose safe rollbacks that honor dedicated capacity and routing fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Status strip fits into existing cluster header without increasing header height
Egress cards show current spend, 24h trend sparkline, forecast for next 2h, and risk band
Canary shield CTA disables canary traffic and triggers a rollback modal with pre-populated rationale
Design includes mobile/tablet responsive variants for on-call use
Figma prototypes and Confluence spec linked and reviewed by PM/ENG
Accessibility: color contrast and keyboard focus states verified
comments: 2026-03-02 - Ethan Clark: Initial concept sketches uploaded to Figma. Two variants: compact strip + expanded card drawer. Noted constraint: cluster header cannot exceed 68px on small viewports.

2026-03-04 - Lina Gómez: Visually prefer the compact strip with hover-to-expand behaviour. PM wants explicit risk band colors tied to billing thresholds. Requesting inclusion of a forecast algorithm summary for accuracy expectations.

2026-03-05 - Samir Patel (ENG): Backend can expose egress burn and forecast in v2 of the metrics API. Need schema: current_bytes, 1h_rate, forecast_2h, billing_bucket_id. Dependency ticket created ENG-82411. Also flagged that real-time streaming may be 10s delayed.

2026-03-07 - Mei Huang (PM): Customer ask from ACME Platform: they want an automated canary freeze that also mutes alerts for the canary window. PM recommends adding an optional checkbox in the rollback modal to 'suppress canary alerts for 30m'.

2026-03-09 - Design Review (Lina, Ethan, Samir, Mei): Agreed on primary CTA: 'Pause Canary'. Secondary actions: 'Rollback to previous' and 'Open Incident Playbook'. Accessibility checks to be scheduled. Action: produce high-fidelity modal and an expanded card showing historical 7d burn.

2026-03-11 - Security Review Request: security_review_required flagged. Need note on when rollback actions are audited in KMS/HSM logs and whether RBAC prevents tenant-level rollbacks. Assigned to security for sign-off.

2026-03-12 - Ethan Clark: Uploaded final HIG adjustments. Provided copy alternatives for microcopy: 'Pause Canary' vs 'Quarantine Canary'. Chosen: 'Pause Canary' for clarity. Ready for engineering estimation and accessibility pass.
design_decisions: Use a compact status strip with three concise indicators: Egress (currency), Risk (low/medium/high), Canary State (running/paused)
Color system maps to billing risk thresholds rather than purely percentiles to reduce false positives
Primary action is non-destructive: 'Pause Canary' performs soft-stop, preserves state, and logs action to audit trail
Fallback UX: if metrics lag > 60s, show a staleness hint and disable auto-forecast UI
